messages.subject: df=1 with Binary Exogenous Variable - fitMeasures
parts:
Hello LAVAANers,

I am running a latent change score model using "sem.mi" where I am adjusting for age (continuous) and gender (binary) on the Time 1 variable, mediator, and latent change score. Model specification includes the use of "fixed.x=TRUE" and I use the syntax "sem.mi(model, data=impList,fixed.x=T,estimator="mlr"). However, using "fitmeasures(model, test="D2") results in one degree of freedom and a chi-square = 0, which seems unlikely. Any help would be appreciated to understand these results.

chisq                   df               pvalue                 ariv                  fmi                 npar

0.000                1.000                1.000                0.000                0.000               72.000


Thank You,

David

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: df=1 with Binary Exogenous Variable - fitMeasures
parts: using "fitmeasures(model, test="D2") results in one degree of freedom and a chi-square = 0, which seems unlikely

But not impossible.  Sometimes pooled statistics are negative (a common problem with the D3 method), in which case I return 0.  Not sure how implausible this is for your data, but you could check your fit statistic in each imputation to see how implausible it is.  You can also pass your set of fit statistics directly to the calculateD2() function to verify.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Non-MI:

                       data = main.3.meaning,

                       missing="FIML",

                       meanstructure = T,

                       int.ov.free = T,fixed.x=T)

Again, runMI() internally sets fixed.x=FALSE.   Your earlier script freed one exogenous variance (age) but not the other (gender), so I am not sure what is happening in your models.  Try comparing your parTable()s to see how they differ (e.g., in the $exo and $free columns).  You can use lav_partable_df() to check the df for the parameter table from each output.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
